content.text: {"title":"The Roof Garden Invitation Parade","premise":"On a sunny roof garden, Ada and Pip, a young dragon, must deliver invitations to three rooftop neighbors before the garden party begins. Pip desperately wants to help, but his warm breath, a gusty roof, and one very confusing invitation create three different problems. The story follows what they actually do, not a preselected route.","cast_and_props":"Ada (wants a splendid party and trusts Pip, but worries about fragile invitations); Pip (wants to be useful and perform a grand delivery); Mrs. Bean, a neighbor and possible guest (wants to know whether the party is quiet or musical). Props: a lidded invitation tin, three paper invitations with colored marks, a string line between chimneys, a blue feather, and a tiny brass bell. Shared setting: the roof garden, with planters, a low wall, and three visible neighboring roofs. State slots include ada.memes.Curiosity, ada.knows.<fact>, pip.memes.Helpfulness, pip.belief.<fact>, invitation*.owner/location/mark, tin.open, bell.rung, mrsbean.agreed, party.mode, party.performed, and audience.response.","kernels_and_interactions":"Use four kernel families: (1) observe/tell knowledge: Ada observes the invitation marks or learns that Mrs. Bean prefers a quiet gathering; telling Pip enables a safe or suitable choice. (2) transfer/access: Ada gives Pip the tin or a marked invitation only after deciding he can carry it. (3) physical delivery: invitations move between Ada, Pip, and named roofs; a delivered invitation changes its location and recipient agreement. (4) performance/response: Pip performs either a soft bell-and-tail parade or a windy sky-dance, and Mrs. Bean responds differently. The three initial problems are: A) a gust has mixed the colored invitations, so Pip believes the blue mark means “music” and carries the wrong invitation; consequence: a silly but successful musical invitation reaches Mrs. Bean, who agrees only if the party becomes a quiet concert. B) Pip’s warm breath has curled one fragile invitation before anyone notices; Ada must learn which paper is still readable and choose a ribbon-tethered hand delivery; consequence: Pip earns trust by carrying the invitation without breathing, and the party becomes a careful ribbon parade. C) Ada assumes Mrs. Bean wants a noisy dragon show, while Mrs. Bean actually wants a peaceful plant breakfast; telling Pip the preference changes his performance; consequence: his silent flower-and-feather performance wins her agreement. Each problem has different final mode, delivery pattern, and audience response. Reuse scenes such as opening the tin, noticing the roof line, asking Mrs. Bean, and performing the final greeting across paths.","seed_parameters":"build(seed) should use a seeded RNG to choose one of three initial configurations, never a route number: mixed_marks=True yields Problem A; curled_invitation=True yields Problem B; mrsbean.preference='quiet' with ada.belief.mrsbean_preference='music' yields Problem C. Keep all state scalar. Initial premise keys: invitation.blue.location, invitation.red.condition, ada.belief.mrsbean_preference, pip.belief.safe_carry. Outcome keys: invitations.delivered, party.mode, party.performed, mrsbean.response. The goal requires at least one invitation delivered, Mrs. Bean’s agreement, and an actual performance. Use 12–18 candidate scenes and select roughly 5–9. Mark only learn_mrsbean_preference and pip_changes_performance as pivotal.","candidate_scenes":"Candidates: open_tin; observe_marks; tell_pip_marks; choose_invitation; transfer_tin; carry_to_blue_roof; discover_curled_paper; observe_readable_mark; tie_ribbon; transfer_ribbon_invitation; ask_mrsbean; observe_mrsbean_preference; tell_pip_preference; deliver_invitation; ring_bell; perform_quiet_flower_parade; perform_windy_tail_dance; mrsbean_agrees_quiet; mrsbean_agrees_music; mrsbean_responds. Reuse open_tin, ask_mrsbean, deliver_invitation, and one final performance scene in materially different paths. Observation must enable choosing the invitation or performance; transfer must enable carrying; delivery must precede agreement; agreement must precede performance.","constraints":"Declare every slot before use, including knowledge paths created by observe/tell. No abstract counters. Guard actions with locations, ownership, knowledge, and motives. Do not let Pip speak as if he knows Mrs. Bean’s preference until told. Every candidate needs a catalog scene card, including preview-only alternatives. Opening variants must be guarded by the actual seed configuration and name the concrete problem. Beat cards should show discovery, dialogue, and the changed choice; bridge cards should connect carrying and routine roof actions. Keep prose warm and comic: Pip practices holding his breath so hard that his cheeks look like two tomatoes. Endings must show different physical/social results rather than explain a lesson.","different_endings":"1. Quiet Ribbon Parade: the invitations hang safely from the string, Pip performs a silent flower-and-feather dance, and Mrs. Bean opens her roof door with a watering can held like a royal trumpet. 2. Musical Misdelivery: the wrongly marked invitation leads to a tiny bell concert; Mrs. Bean agrees, and Pip’s tail keeps time against the chimney pots. 3. Gentle Dragon Greeting: after learning Mrs. Bean wanted peace, Pip performs without flame or roar, nudging a blue feather across the roof; Mrs. Bean places a teacup beside the invitation and joins the party. Provide at least two prose variants for each ending, with conditions on party.mode, party.performed, and mrsbean.response; never mention unused props or alternate outcomes."}
